html:
A burst of sweeping reforms in Joseon Korea from 1894 to 1896, pushed through by a reform cabinet under strong Japanese pressure. It ended much of Korea's old social order.

It began in the crisis of 1894. The Donghak peasant revolt drew Chinese and Japanese troops into Korea. Japanese soldiers occupied the royal palace and put in a cabinet of Korean reformers under Kim Hong-jip.

Among its many measures:

  • the legal class system, which had put the yangban aristocracy above commoners, was abolished;
  • slavery and the buying and selling of people were ended;
  • the old civil service exams were abolished;
  • widows were allowed to remarry and early marriage was banned;
  • official documents began to use Hangul;
  • Korea ended its tribute ties to Qing China.

A rule that men cut off their topknots in 1895 caused fury, and Japanese agents murdered Queen Min that year. In 1896 King Gojong fled to the Russian legation, the reform cabinet fell and Kim was killed by a mob. Many of the changes stayed.
sum: A burst of sweeping reforms in Joseon Korea from 1894 to 1896, pushed through by a reform cabinet under strong Japanese pressure. It ended much of Korea's old social order.
